emotional weather

How does setting make a reader feel?

Recall 5 · Scale 10 · Annotate 20 · Transform 15 · Exit 5
0–5 · Sensory recall

Rebuild this place through the body

Record one concrete detail for each sense. Circle the detail that most controls the mood.

Learning intention

Analyse how setting and sensory imagery create mood.

1Select a short setting detail
2Name the sense and precise mood
3Explain the causal bridge
4Develop one effect paragraph
Vocabulary

Mood is not the same as emotion

Character emotion

What a person in the story feels.

Reader mood

The atmosphere the writing creates for us.

If Margot is sad, must the whole passage feel sad? No. Setting, sound, rhythm and contrast shape the reader’s mood.

5–15 · Mood scale

From constricting to expansive

oppressivebleakuneasyanticipatoryexhilaratedwonder-filled

Place, challenge, justify. There is no credit for silent guessing.

Rapid check · 1/3

Continuous rain and enclosed waiting

oppressive · the weather feels relentless and difficult to escape.

Rapid check · 2/3

The hush before the door opens

anticipatory · withheld sound stretches expectation. Uneasy is also defensible.

Rapid check · 3/3

The first rush into sunlight

wonder-filled · warmth, colour and rarity create awe; exhilarated also fits.

Model the method

Four questions. One chain.

DETAIL

smallest phrase

→
SENSE / CHOICE

what do we experience?

→
MOOD

exact shade

→
BECAUSE

why does it feel that way?

Precision check

Which annotation actually analyses?

Tap each card to expose the diagnosis.

Partner protocol

Select. Challenge. Swap.

  1. Partner A selects the smallest useful phrase.
  2. Partner B asks: “Why that word? Why that mood?”
  3. Complete one row.
  4. Swap roles for the next anchor.

Star the row that gives you most to explain.

Midpoint check

Improve the foggy sentence

“The rain creates a sad mood because it is raining.”
35–50 · Weather Alchemy

The rain fell on the school.

Keep the event. Change the reader.

oppressive
Craft controls

Choose; do not decorate

precise verbsoundtexturemovementcomparisonsentence rhythm

Two choices working together beat six techniques fighting each other.

Model transformation

Target: oppressive

Rain hammered the roof and pressed its grey weight against every window.

Sound + personified pressure make the building feel trapped. The mood comes from the relationship between choices—not the number of devices.

exact word / phrase

→
SENSORY IMPRESSION

hear, feel or see

Bradbury creates a/an [precise mood] atmosphere when… The phrase “…” appeals to [sense] through [choice]. This makes the setting seem [interpretation], so the reader [effect]. This matters because [situation / contrast].
